IS 18366: 2023 
Physiograph 
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) recently adopted a standard related to physiographs, 
following the approval of the draft by the Anatomy and Forensic Sciences Equipment Sectional 
Committee and subsequent endorsement by the Medical Equipment and Hospital Planning 
Division Council. This standard establishes guidelines for the utilization of physiographs, 
devices employed for recording physiological parameters in both human and animal subjects. 
This standard delineates the specifications for physiographs and underscores their role in 
recording physiological data. These devices, equipped with specialized application programs, 
offer a versatile data recording and analysis system when employed in conjunction with 
compatible computers. However, it is imperative to note that the use of physiographs is 
restricted to teaching and research applications and environments exclusively. 
A key emphasis within the standard is the necessity for individuals utilizing physiographs to 
possess experience and awareness of experimental protocols. Additionally, a thorough 
understanding of human and animal safety measures is deemed essential to prevent any harm 
during experiments. Notably, the standard explicitly states that physiographs are not intended 
for diagnosing, treating, or monitoring subjects in hospital or domestic settings. Furthermore, 
their use is not directed towards the prevention, curing, or alleviation of diseases, injuries, or 
handicaps. 
To ensure the appropriate installation, operation, and use of physiographs, the standard 
mandates supervision by an appropriately qualified life-science researcher. The typical usage 
environment is identified as a research or teaching lab, or a hospital. Environmental factors 
such as temperature, humidity, ventilation, noise intensity, and light intensity must be 
maintained at suitable levels, as these may contribute to the levels of mouse anxiety, 
particularly relevant in experimental studies involving rodents. 
The Committee responsible for formulating this standard conducted a thorough review of 
international standards and other publications. Among the accepted standards is the 
International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standard IEC 61326-1:2020. This standard, 
titled "Electrical equipment for measurement, control and laboratory use — EMC requirements 
— Part 1: General requirements". Strict adherence to the test methods described therein is 
mandated, and these procedures are intended for use by individuals who have been adequately 
trained and are competent in performing them.
